h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אִיָּר, א׳ Rosh Chodesh Iyar, 1
The Month of Ziv: The Avos' Radiance and the Preparation for Matan Torah

p: It is stated in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 11a):
From where do we know that the Avos were born in Nissan?
"And it was..." in the month of Ziv,
the month in which were born
the radiant ones of the world.
they had already been born, in Nissan.
This needs explanation: according to this,
why is the month of Iyar called Ziv?
Since they were born in Nissan,
הֲוָה לֵיהּ לִקְרוֹת חוֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן זִיו
the month of Nissan should have been called Ziv!
as we have said many times,
that the main light of the month
And for this reason it is called "Rosh Chodesh,"
and not "the first of the month" —
because it is the head of the month,
and everything follows after the head.
And since the Avos were born
is called the month of Ziv.
after all, the months are reckoned
אַךְ הַחוֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים
But "This month shall be for you the head of the months" —
counting by the months of the moon —
was first instituted at Yetzias Mitzrayim,
when the Jewish nation was founded;
since they counted by the sun then;
when the Jewish nation came into being,
the month of Iyar was called Ziv,
the light of the Avos was already present.
And all the Avos are the light of the sun,
that was created on the first day,
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham."
And the primordial light was created
מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ (חֲגִיגָה יב, א)
from one end of the world to the other (Chagigah 12a).
Afterwards, when it was hidden away
and the luminaries were created on the fourth day,
the light of the sun receives
and the moon receives from the light of the sun.
As it says of the future (Yeshayahu 30:26):
"And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun,
and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold,
like the light of the seven days."
"like the light of the seven days" —
which comes to three hundred forty-three
וְהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ הוּא חֵלֶק קָטָן מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
and the sun is only a small part of the primordial light.
it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 95:3):
And the essence of light is the Torah,
as it says (Mishlei 6:23), "And Torah is light."
is written in the utterance "Let there be light"
correspond to the five Chumashim of the Torah
the sun has come, the sun has come, etc.
Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?"
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ו, ט)
And this is the meaning of what Chazal said (Bereishis Rabbah 6:9),
are you not my father's purchase?
לֹא כָּךְ רָאָה אוֹתְךָ אַבָּא בַּחֲלוֹם
Did not my father see you so in a dream:
what kind of claim is it
that the one likened to the sun
for whose sake the primordial light was hidden away,
as stated in the Zohar HaKadosh
זָרַע לֵיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
the Holy One, blessed be He, sowed it...
who is the gardener of the garden...
And the sun receives its light
that is hidden away for the tzaddikim.
And this is what Yehoshua said to the sun:
which is the "light sown for the tzaddik."
the sun receives from this light,
and the moon receives from the light of the sun.
And this is why it is called the month of Ziv:
when the Jewish nation was formed,
the light of the Avos was already present.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 11a — "Rabbi Yehoshua says: From where do we know that the Avos were born in Nissan? For it says, 'And it was in the four hundred and eightieth year… in the month of Ziv' (I Melachim 6:1) — in the month in which the radiant ones (zivtanei) of the world were born."

paragraphs.text: Rashi, Rosh Hashanah 11a (s.v. shenoldu) — "'In the month of Ziv' — this is Iyar. 'In which the radiant ones of the world were born' — when Iyar began, they had already been born in Nissan. Alternatively: sometimes the solar Nissan extends into the lunar Iyar."

rich.text: — "'In the month of Ziv' — this is Iyar. 'In which the radiant ones of the world were born' — when Iyar began, they had already been born in Nissan. Alternatively: sometimes the solar Nissan extends into the lunar Iyar."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Rosh Hashanah 11a — “Those born in Nissan were not complete in their birth, to be counted among the born, until after thirty days, which fall in Iyar. Therefore the Avos, who are the radiance of the world — since their thirty days were completed in Iyar, this radiance is ascribed to Iyar, and so Iyar is called ‘the month of Ziv,’ for their birth was completed in it. And according to the one who says it is called Ziv ‘because it has radiance for the trees’: the blossom comes out in Nissan and covers the body of the fruit, which is the tree's radiance; in Iyar the blossom falls and the body of the fruit is seen.” Connection: He too asks why the Avos' radiance belongs to Iyar rather than Nissan, and answers that what begins in Nissan is completed and revealed only in Iyar.

paragraphs.text: Targum Yonasan, Yeshayahu 30:26 — "And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun is destined to shine three hundred and forty-three times over, like the light of the seven days [of Creation]."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 166b — “The Holy One, blessed be He, sowed this light in His Garden of Eden, making it row upon row through that righteous one who is the garden's gardener. He takes this light, sows it as a seed of truth, and makes it row upon row in the garden; it gives birth, sprouts, and makes fruit, from which the world is nourished. This is 'Light is sown for the righteous.' ... These are the seeds of the first light, continually sown: now they give birth and make fruit, and now they are being sown. Before the world eats this fruit, that seed already gives birth and yields further fruit, without ceasing.” The gardener receives and plants the primordial light, rather than originating it. This is the precise connection with Yosef transmitting illumination to Malchus.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 18 — “The light is the aspect of the first light that was hidden… and the sun, whose body is fire, is as the first light was before it was hidden. The nations count by the sun as it is now, in its sheath; but of the future it is written, ‘The light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun’ (Yeshayahu 30:26). It follows that the sun in this world is truly only an aspect of light, like the moon that receives from the light of the sun.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the sun receives from the hidden light”; both read the moon's future light through the sun that itself receives.

because it has radiance for the trees.
We need to understand the reason
by the name Ziv in the pasuk,
for in the pesukim we do not find
since the names of the months came up from Bavel
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה א, ב
Only regarding the building of the Beis HaMikdash
Now Tishrei, "the month of the Eisanim" —
which the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah ibid.) explains
means they are strong in mitzvos —
it is understandable to give it a special name.
why was it given the special name Ziv
are the words of the Living God,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים כ, יט)
in the way of what is said (Devarim 20:19):
"For man is a tree of the field."
And in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:17):
To a prince who recovered from his illness.
His tutor said to the king,
עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא בְּנִי לְזִיווֹ וְכוּלֵּי
"My son has not yet regained his radiance..."
there were among them people with blemishes
from the bondage of mortar and bricks...
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them:
עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא זִיוָתָן שֶׁל בָּנַי
"My children's radiance has not yet returned
from the bondage of mortar and bricks.
Let My children be refreshed for three months,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֶתֵּן לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵּי
and afterwards I will give them the Torah..."
that Yisrael were healed until Matan Torah,
when all those with blemishes were healed,
מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהֶן סוּמִין וְכוּלֵּי
"From where do we know there were no blind among them...
that there were no deaf among them..."
And the Torah is "healing to all his flesh,"
אֵין צָרִיךְ זְמַן שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים לְרַפְּאוֹתָן
does not need three months to heal them;
"And the Egyptians did evil to us" —
to the point that it says (ibid. 4:34),
"a nation from the midst of a nation,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כג, ב)
as stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 23:2);
and they needed to be purified
עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא זִיוָתָן שֶׁל בָּנַי
"My children's radiance has not yet come,"
from when it puts forth its blossom
they received in the month of Sivan,
was the preparation for Matan Torah.
And this is what they meant:
that the radiance of My children would come.
the month of Iyar is called Ziv,
because it has radiance for the trees —
"man is a tree of the field."
And although the time when the trees blossom
is in the days of Nissan
was the time of Yetzias Mitzrayim,
and likewise the Avos were born in Nissan —
the month of Iyar was given to them
as the one that brings the radiance of My children.
at the time the Beis HaMikdash was built,
it was called the month of Ziv.
For in truth the building of the Beis HaMikdash
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ה

which is the desire of the heart

in the month of Iyar before Sivan,

And about this he said (Shir HaShirim 2:5),
that they are still sick with love.

the Written Torah and the Oral Torah."

and of the Oral Torah, too,

talmidei chachamim, whose whole body is fire

the Written Torah, the Oral Torah,"

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 7 — “‘The King said: My son has not yet regained his radiance (ziv)… so the Holy One said: the radiance of My children has not yet come, from the bondage of mortar and bricks; rather, let them be refreshed…’ Ziv is the attribute of Yosef the tzaddik… as the Zohar (III 117b) says, he is the radiance of the blessings, from whom radiance goes out to the world, and therefore it is called the month of Ziv. Surely it does not mean that they were to be healed of the blemishes from the bondage, for Hashem could heal them in a moment; rather, their radiance had not yet come, for they had not yet been refined in the attribute of Ziv, Yesod, through the counting of seven times seven.” Connection: Rav Tzadok reads the same Midrash there as the Sefirah's refinement leading to Matan Torah, tying it to the name Ziv as he does here.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Yisro 8 — "When Israel left Egypt there were among them people with blemishes from the crushing labor… The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Is it right that I give My Torah to people with blemishes? He signaled to the ministering angels, and they came down and healed them. From where do we know there were no blind among them? 'And all the people saw the sounds' (Shemos 20:15). And no deaf? For they said, 'We will do and we will hear.'"

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 27a — "Rabbi Abbahu said: The fire of Gehinnom has no power over Torah scholars. It is a kal vachomer from the salamander: if one who anoints himself with the blood of the salamander, which is a creature of fire, is not harmed by fire, then Torah scholars, whose whole body is fire — as it is written, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29) — all the more so."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 40a (Shemini) — "The ashishah brings in the wine; the apple draws out the wine and directs the will. Therefore 'with ashishos and apples': ashishos — to be sated with wine; apples — to direct the will, so that the wine should do no harm. And all this, why? 'For I am lovesick' — in exile."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 2a — “‘Ask for yourself a sign’—an actual letter, for all was carried through the mystery of letters. Of Rachav it says, ‘Give me a true sign’: This is the letter Vav, which is called the letter of truth. Are the other letters not truth? They are, but this letter is called the letter of truth.” The maamar joins the designation of Vav with “Give truth to Yaakov,” identifying the patriarchal quality within the letter.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 122b (Ra'aya Meheimna) — "Two letters awaken a person to Torah and mitzvah. Yud is fear: it rests upon a person's head, and from it fear enters his heart to fear the Holy One, blessed be He… Hei is love… And Vav rests upon a person's head, and from it there enter into his mouth words with which to study Torah."
